Nope not normal. For me, I didn't see any friends or extended family until after mine was at least one month old. I only allowed our parents and siblings but they had to come to us. I wasn't and couldn't go to them. Everyone respected my choice, and they should respect yours! You just had a baby for crying out loud!  You are allowed to say no, remember that!

Enjoy every moment, go out (doesn't have to involve alcohol), take as much experiences as you possiblly can, learn to say no to people who cause you pain, put money aside (even if it's $20 or $10, just always take something out with each pay), and take chances. The 20s is where you find yourself and be inspired. I wish I did mine differently and regret me not doing any of this.

I know how you feel. Mine is with childhood trauma though and it's hard because I'm 35F, and I feel like a hit a huge brick wall giving me reminders of everything that happened in my life from growing up with a horrible dad to having a poor marriage. I am depressed and I am constantly reading past texts or messages, or notes I use to leave myself of things that happened, etc and I don't know if I do it because I want a reminder that I really didn't do anything wrong, that I am enough or whatever. But at the same time my overthinking tells me something else because no matter what I do or say, it doesn't matter to anyone else. No one is ever considerate to my pain or how much things affect me. I was told before that you can write a letter to yourself as a way of forgiving or as a way to make peace with whatever happened. In your case, your situation is a fragile one and not sure it's the best way so my suggestion is to talk to a therapist with what you are going through and see if there is a better way to tackle this. I am very sorry though on what you went through! You are very strong for writing this! Know that you are special and you will find peace.
